concept: TransferList is two printed lists on one panel, the rows that are available and the rows that are chosen, with a column of keys between them that carries the marked rows across. Like a patch field on a Braun hi-fi, nothing is dragged: you mark, press a named key, and the row stands in its new window.

default_to_avoid.pattern: transfer list as two bordered boxes with checkboxes in every row and arrow buttons filled blue
default_to_avoid.why_not: A checkbox in each row repeats a mechanism the Listbox already marks with a tick, and a blue key spends the hue that P1 keeps for one part per unit.

default_to_avoid.pattern: dual list that moves rows only by dragging them from one box to the other
default_to_avoid.why_not: Dragging cannot be reached from a keyboard or a screen reader, so the mechanism has no key map and rows cannot be moved by everyone.

references.source: Braun Studio 1 hi-fi (Dieter Rams, 1957): two banks of printed sources with the patch keys set between them on the case
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): the bands printed in one window and the chosen band marked in another
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: listbox pattern, multiple selection with a move button (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/listbox/examples/listbox-rearrangeable/)
Listbox in this system: each window is a multiple Listbox, imported and not redrawn

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: Each side is a Listbox, so both lists are windows of surface.sunken with elevation.well and a line.ring hairline, cut into the same body and equal in size.

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: A polite status says how many rows moved and where, then how many are available and chosen; it is printed nowhere else and takes no focus.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The move keys are round 44px IconButtons named in words, with the same gap as the rows, so a thumb finds one without touching its neighbour.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Space marks a row in a list, Tab reaches the key and Enter presses it, and Alt with the arrow toward the other list moves the marked rows without leaving the list.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: Each list is named by a printed label above its window on the inset line, with its count under the window on the same line.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: Both windows keep the same size and the keys keep their column, so a move changes the rows inside the windows and nothing else.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The keys are body-coloured keys and a marked row is a tick and weight, so the unit's one orange stays free for the key that saves the choice.

options.name: two windows side by side with a column of round keys between them
two windows with word keys printed under each window
two windows stacked with one row of keys between them

variants.reason: A puts the keys on the line between the lists, so the direction of each key matches the direction the row travels and the keys read as a patch column in black and white (P3 interaction, P6 space); B splits the keys into four word capsules that wrap in other languages, and C is kept as the narrow layout of A, because side by side does not fit a phone.

root.why: The two lists and the key column sit in one row, and the row wraps into a stack only when the width cannot hold them, so nothing moves between states.

column.why: A list, its label and its count stack in one column on the same inset line, so both sides read the same way.

caption.why: The count under each window uses the caption size in secondary ink, a plain printed line with a tabular figure that does not shift as rows move.

keys.why: The keys stand in one column on the middle line, 44px apart from their neighbours, and turn into a row when the lists stack.

key.why: Each key is the round 44px key of the control class with one printed arrow, and a key with no rows to carry fades like any disabled part.

pair.why: The keys that move every row print two arrows side by side, so a sighted person tells all from marked without reading the name.

md.why: Both windows keep the height of six 44px rows whatever they hold, so a move never changes the size of the unit.

lg.why: Both windows keep the height of six 52px rows for a phone sheet, so a move never changes the size of the unit.

data-stacked=true.why: When the width holds only one window the lists stack and the keys lie in a row between them, with arrows turned to point down and up.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the keys keep a real border in the text colour, so each stays a visible target, while the windows come from Listbox.
